name: Token Latency Fairness: Performance Isolation for Multi-Tenant LLM Serving
problem: Existing multi-tenant isolation equalises client THROUGHPUT over the long run (queueing/batching fairness) but gives no LATENCY guarantee, so a well-behaved client can still see its token-level latency badly degraded by a noisy neighbour.
mechanism: Introduce a delta-token fairness guarantee: for a well-behaved client, a token that takes d time units in isolation is produced within d + delta under multi-tenant execution. The scheduler enforces per-token deadlines while bounding delay from GPU compute sharing AND from the extra delay that shared KV caching introduces — the KV sharing term is the hard part, since it couples tenants without any scheduling action.
speedup_reported: NOT RECORDED as a multiple — the abstract states the delta-token guarantee qualitatively without a verified headline figure carrying baseline and settings. The paper's contribution is the GUARANTEE, not a speedup: throughput fairness and latency isolation are being traded against each other and a 'speedup' framing would be misleading here.
notes: Venue arxiv-preprint: no venue in the arXiv comment. Included because it names the failure mode every shared serving tier hits — long-run throughput fairness is NOT latency isolation — and because a delta-parameterised latency guarantee is the kind of claim that, if it holds, changes what you can sell as a multi-tenant service. The Zaharia/Krieger Berkeley lineage makes the provenance credible but the result is unreviewed as of this record.
